taxmill 0.1.0
  • Get started
  • Reference

Experimental. A mill for digital PDF financial statements: text out, a manual pass to shape the lines, and one tidy Excel workbook in. Tax accounts and ordinary annual accounts both work, because both are laid out as tables. Grown out of the accounts statistics at Statistics Greenland, by way of daos, where it started as a handful of helpers.

Installation 

pak::pak("dataniel/taxmill")

The three steps 

library(taxmill)

accounts_pdf_to_txt("data/pdf", "data/txt")

# ... shape the statements into category and data lines by hand ...

accounts_txt_to_xlsx("data/txt", "data/accounts.xlsx", year = 2024)

Nothing leaves the machine

The documents this package is pointed at are usually confidential — a tax account is not a published annual report. So there is no upload, no API call, and no service in the loop. accounts_pdf_to_txt() reads local PDFs and writes local text files; accounts_txt_to_xlsx() reads those and writes one workbook. That is the whole surface.

Why the middle step is manual

A PDF financial statement is a table whose structure lives in the layout, not in the file, and the line labels differ between preparers. A parser that guessed would produce numbers that look right and are wrong — which is worse than no numbers, because nothing downstream would flag them. Shaping the lines is the point at which a person decides what the table actually says.

What the package does is make everything around that step cheap:

  • Extraction is one call over a whole directory.
  • PDFs with no extractable text — scans, photographs — are skipped with a warning and no .txt file. The function will not pretend it read them.
  • Validation problems are collected across all files and reported together at the end, so one malformed line in the twentieth file does not cost you nineteen files’ worth of feedback. Nothing is written until every file has passed.

vignette("taxmill") documents the text-file format exactly.

If you do not have the PDFs yet

For published Danish annual reports, cvrr searches Erhvervsstyrelsens distribution service and downloads them; point accounts_pdf_to_txt() at the directory it filled.

And check whether the filing exists as XBRL first. If it does, cvrr::read_xbrl() parses it straight into a tibble with no manual step at all. The mill is for the filings with no machine-readable form — older reports, small companies, and anything that began life on paper.

Functions

Function Description
accounts_pdf_to_txt() Convert PDF financial statements to text files
accounts_txt_to_xlsx() Parse shaped text files and export to Excel, validated first
